                <h2 class="text-h3 font-bold hyphens text-center mb-4 md:mb-2">Bridging traditional divides at the TUM School of Management</h2>
            
            
                <p class="text-body1 hyphens text-center mb-8">TUM School of Management, firmly rooted within TUM&#039;s technological and entrepreneurial ecosystem, places a unique focus on the interface between management, engineering, and the natural and life sciences. The School&#039;s goal is to bridge the traditional divide between the fields of management and technology.</p>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Master&#039;s program in Finance and Information Management ranks 1st in Germany and 31st worldwide</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>In the 2027 QS Business Masters Rankings, TUM School of Management's Masters program in Finance and Information Management was rated for the first time and ended up on place 31st among the 286 ranked Master of Finance programs globally, which makes it the<strong> Top 1 in Germany</strong>. The Master’s in Management &amp; Technology was able to maintain its position as 28th out of 256 programs in the Master in Management category worldwide and therefore remains one of the<strong> Top 3 programs in Germany</strong>.<br><br>TUM School of Management has demonstrated its excellence, with both programs ranking above average across all five evaluation categories: <strong>employability, thought leadership, value for money, alumni outcomes, and diversity</strong>. This recognition highlights our dedication to providing a world-class educational experience that prepares students for successful careers, contributes to cutting-edge management research, delivers strong value for investment, supports graduates in achieving outstanding professional outcomes, and fosters a diverse and inclusive community that enriches learning and innovation.<br><br>We are honored by this recognition, which underscores the strength of our interdisciplinary approach in bringing together diverse expertise and perspectives to accelerate sustainable innovation and shape future ecosystems.</p></div>

                                    <div class="text-content relative pl-8 pt-8 pb-6 pr-6 h-[356px] md:h-[320px] overflow-hidden transition-all duration-500 ease-in-out">
                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">European Private Equity Research Symposium 2026</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>The CEFS at TUM School of Management, led by its scientific directors Ann-Kristin Achleitner, Reiner Braun and Christoph Kaserer, hosted the European Private Equity Research Symposium on 10 and 11 September, together with its partner the Institute for Private Capital. Munich joins Chapel Hill, Oxford and Singapore in the series.</p>
<p>The format is the point. Every paper is followed by a panel that takes it to the people who act on it.</p>
<p>Research presentations by Christian Lundblad (UNC Kenan-Flagler) on buyout fund exits and distributions, Ludovic Phalippou (University of Oxford) on continuation vehicles as strategic asset transfers, Juha Joenväärä (Aalto University) on benchmarking private credit, and Florencio Lopez-de-Silanes (SKEMA Business School) on private equity intermediary performance reports. For the keynote, Tim Jenkinson (University of Oxford) on whether private equity firms allocate capital according to manager skill.</p>
<p>Four panels led by experts in practice:</p>
<p>Liquidity and Risk Premia in Private Markets, moderated by Ferdinand Seibert, with Malte Frederichs (YIELCO Investments), Mark Jansen (University of Utah) and Roger Vincent&nbsp;(Summation Capital).</p>
<p>Who Sets the Price? Valuation, Governance and Trust in GP-Led Deals, moderated by Stefan Morkötter (University of St. Gallen), with Oleg Gredil (Tulane University), Andreas Kumeth (PAI Partners) and Christoph Schemmerl (Golding Capital Partners).</p>
<p>The Evolving Role of Private Credit, moderated by Greg Brown, with Jason Amoratis (MSCI), Raluca Jochmann (Allianz Global Investors), and Verena Kempe (KENFO).</p>
<p>Private Markets in the Age of AI, moderated by Reiner Braun, with Andrea Carnelli Dompe (Tamarix), Borja Fernández Tamayo (Sagard), and Julien Perez (Bpifrance).</p>
<p>Organised by Reiner Braun and Sara Boni at the CEFS, with Greg Brown and Sarah Franks at the Institute for Private Capital. Thanks to every speaker, panelist, and chair, and to everyone who traveled to Munich and kept the conversation going through the breaks. Thank you also to Allianz Asset Management and the UAI Foundation, whose support made this event possible.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">TCU Entrepreneurship Research Ranking</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>Technical University of Munich climbs the global rankings in entrepreneurship research!</p>
<p>In the 2026 TCU Global University Entrepreneurship Research Productivity Rankings, TUM is listed among the Top 2 universities worldwide for research output in leading entrepreneurship journals.</p>
<p>This year’s result marks a jump from fourth to second within just one year, highlighting the growing influence of entrepreneurship research at TUM School of Management, and in particular, TUM Entrepreneurship Research Institute.</p>

<p>A strong recognition of TUM’s global impact and our commitment at TUM School of Management to advancing evidence-based entrepreneurship research.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Large Language Models Empowering Future Industry Workshop 2026</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>Prof. Dr. Ziyue Li hosted the 1st International Workshop on 𝗟𝗮𝗿𝗴𝗲 𝗟𝗮𝗻𝗴𝘂𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗠𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹𝘀 𝗘𝗺𝗽𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗙𝘂𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗜𝗻𝗱𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘆 in Heilbronn on 20–21 July 2026.</p>
<p>Large Language Models are not only a technical shift. They are reshaping how firms organize decisions, structure processes, integrate data, and manage the boundary between human judgment and automated action - questions at the very core of what we teach and research in management.</p>
<p>The workshop had 1 keynote, 8 talks, 1 panel, 1 industry tour at the Innovation Park Artificial Intelligence (IPAI), with speakers from HKUST, Virginia Tech, TU Dortmund, BMW Group, ZF Group, ZETA GmbH, Schneider Electric, AutoScout24, AS-Schneider Group, Lithos AI, AWS, Meta, and Microsoft.</p>
<p>The insights<br>💡 Operationalizing LLMs in industry is a data, process, and integration challenge - not primarily a modeling one.<br>💡 Small open models with careful training and task design can match proprietary frontier performance.<br>💡 Agentic AI in production requires safety-gated execution and meaningful human oversight.<br>💡 Digital twins become useful when the world model reasons back - not when it simply visualizes.</p>
<p>Stay tuned for a workshop White Paper mapping industry's burning challenges to academia's proven LLM solutions, which will follow this autumn.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">TUM School of Management and ETH Zurich Secure SNSF-DFG WEAVE Funding for Joint Research on Virtual Reality</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>The Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) and the German Research Foundation (DFG) are funding a new joint research project by the TUM Professorship of Marketing &amp; Technology at the TUM School of Management and the Chair of Technology Marketing at the Department of Management, Technology, and Economics at ETH Zurich under the WEAVE scheme.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Over the next three years, researchers from the TUM School of Management and ETH Zurich will investigate how people perceive time and space in immersive virtual environments. Immersive environments do not simply reproduce reality; they can reshape how long a moment feels and how near or far things seem. Understanding these mechanisms is increasingly important as virtual spaces become a growing part of how people interact, consume, and work.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>The project brings together perspectives from consumer psychology, technology, and human-computer interaction to examine the cognitive mechanisms underlying time and space perception in virtual reality and their implications for the design, evaluation, and regulation of immersive environments.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>The project is led by <strong>Prof. Dr. David Finken</strong>, <strong>Dr. Thomas Scheurer,</strong> and <strong>Prof. Dr. Florian von Wangenheim</strong> and reflects a close research collaboration between the TUM School of Management and ETH Zurich.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>We congratulate the project team on securing this funding and look forward to the insights and contributions that will emerge from this cross-border collaboration between Germany and Switzerland.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Supply Chain Finance Week 2026 </p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>This June, Prof. David Wuttke hosted the <strong>2nd Supply Chain Finance Week 2026</strong> at TUM Campus Heilbronn, bringing together leading academics for an inspiring exchange on the future of Supply Chain Finance.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>A key highlight of the week was the <strong>Supply Chain &amp; Finance Symposium</strong>, featuring a distinguished international lineup of scholars who shared insights on current trends, emerging challenges, and the future direction of the field. The keynote was delivered by Prof. Chris Tang, Distinguished Professor Emeritus at UCLA Anderson School of Management.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>The symposium also included break-out sessions on a question of real-world relevance: <strong>How can Supply Chain Finance contribute to advancing the UN Sustainable Development Goals? </strong>The discussions were collaborative, in-depth, and thought-provoking.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Another highlight was the <strong>“Meet your Co-Authors”</strong> session, which created dedicated space for individual exchange, ongoing research projects, and new academic collaborations.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>The <strong>Ph.D. and Young Scholar Pitch Session</strong> brought great energy to the room, with doctoral students and early-career researchers presenting their work in concise three-minute pitches that sparked curiosity and discussion.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Furthermore, the participants discussed the <strong>17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) set by the United Nations (UN)</strong> in depth. The focus lay especially on Goal number 13, “Climate Action,” which urges UN members to take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>The week concluded with a Doctoral Day under the theme <strong>“Publishing Supply Chain Finance Research”</strong>, offering young scholars the opportunity to learn from and connect with experienced researchers. Sessions explored what defines impactful empirical Operations Management research, how modelling work can generate meaningful insights, and which mechanisms are central to research in supply chain management and finance.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>A few key takeaways became clear throughout the week:</p><ul><li>Supply Chain Finance research continues to raise the bar in rigor and depth of insight.</li><li>The UN Sustainable Development Goals offer important opportunities for SCF research, but each goal requires deliberate strategies and mechanisms.</li><li>Supply Chain Finance is gaining genuine global attention.</li><li>AI and large language models are becoming increasingly relevant to the future of SCF research.</li></ul><p>A big thank you to all participants, speakers, and contributors who made this week such a success. It was a pleasure to exchange ideas, build connections, and shape the future of Supply Chain Finance — together.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">MEET THE PRESIDENT: Roberta Metsola - Democracy at Work in the European Parliament</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>The Technical University of Munich (TUM) is honored to welcome <strong>Roberta Metsola,</strong> President of the European Parliament, on<strong> June 19, 2026.</strong></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Event:</strong> &nbsp;Meet the President: Democracy at Work in the European Parliament<br><strong>Time:</strong> &nbsp;11:45 AM – 12:45 PM<br><strong>Location: &nbsp;</strong><a href="https://nav.tum.de/room/0509.EG.980" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">Audimax, TUM Main Campus</a></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Moderated by the TUM Speakers Series, President Metsola will share insights into the functioning of European democracy and engage directly with the audience.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>This event offers a unique opportunity to experience European politics up close and take part in an open exchange on current challenges and developments within the European Union.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">TUM ranks among the top European universities for start-ups!</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>TUM ranks among the top European universities for start-ups!</p>
<p>TUM ranks 4th among very large universities for the number of start-ups founded by researchers (38 in 2025), trailing only the University of Oxford, Imperial College London, and the University of Cambridge. With 235 start-ups founded by students and alumni, TUM ranks 8th overall—and is the only very large German university in Europe’s top 20.</p>
<p>TUM stands out due to its strong entrepreneurial ecosystem, which combines excellent research, industry collaboration, and targeted support programs for founders (such as UnternehmerTUM).</p>
<p>A key factor in TUM’s high ranking is the large number of successful companies founded by its students, researchers, and alumni. Many start-ups have grown into internationally active businesses, contributing to economic growth and technological advancement.</p>
<p>“Over the past few years, we have implemented numerous initiatives at TUM specifically designed to strengthen the entrepreneurial spirit in our university’s research and teaching,” says TUM President Prof. Thomas F. Hofmann.</p>
<p>We are very proud of our students, alumni, and researchers!</p></div>

                                    <div class="text-content relative pl-8 pt-8 pb-6 pr-6 h-[356px] md:h-[320px] overflow-hidden transition-all duration-500 ease-in-out">
                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">CHE University Ranking 2026: Students give TUM School of Management top ratings</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>TUM School of Management students are extremely satisfied with the teaching and study conditions in their management studies. In the new ranking by the Center for Higher Education Development (CHE), they give their school in Munich and Heilbronn the best marks.</p>
<p>In business administration, TUM School of Management is at the top of almost all categories. Especially high scores were reached in the category “digital teaching” in Munich (4.6 stars). In Heilbronn, students awarded 4.6 stars for the “rooms” on our modern campus. The categories “variety of courses” and “organization of studies” are praised at both campuses.</p>
<p>Germany's largest university ranking gathers facts and opinions from 120,000 students. The CHE compares individual subjects at German-speaking universities, this time in economics. The ranking is primarily intended to provide prospective students with orientation. The universities are rated across numerous categories on a scale of 1 to 5 stars.</p>
<p>See the full ranking here: <a href="https://studiengaenge.zeit.de/ranking" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">https://studiengaenge.zeit.de/ranking</a></p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Paul Fornoff got elected Global President of the QTEM Student Association</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>Paul Fornoff, a student in the <strong>Master’s in Management and Technology at the TUM School of Management,</strong> got elected Global President of the QTEM Student Association. He has been a member of the QTEM network since 2024.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>In his role as Global President, Paul Fornoff supports the coordination of student activities across the QTEM network and works with the international executive team on initiatives aimed at strengthening QTEM’s global presence and fostering engagement with students and strategic partners.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><i>“I am honoured to take on this role and excited to serve the QTEM community. Together with my team, we are launching initiatives to strengthen our global presence and engage the next generation of students and partners,”</i> says Paul Fornoff.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>His appointment reflects the active involvement of TUM School of Management students within the QTEM network and their contribution to its continued development.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Katinka Kleinheinz appointed as Managing Director of the TUM School of Management</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>As of March 1, 2026, <strong>Katinka Kleinheinz</strong> has assumed the position of <strong>Managing Director </strong>at the<strong> TUM School of Management</strong>. She has been part of the School since 2017 and most recently served as Director of Undergraduate and Postgraduate Education, where she made significant contributions to the development and strategic direction of our study programs.</p>

                                    <div class="text-content relative pl-8 pt-8 pb-6 pr-6 h-[356px] md:h-[320px] overflow-hidden transition-all duration-500 ease-in-out">
                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">TUM recognized as a University of Excellence for the fourth consecutive time</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>The <a href="https://www.tum.de/en/news-and-events/all-news/press-releases/details/tum-recognized-as-university-of-excellence-for-the-fourth-consecutive-time" target="_blank" class="fui-Link ___1q1shib f2hkw1w f3rmtva f1ewtqcl fyind8e f1k6fduh f1w7gpdv fk6fouc fjoy568 figsok6 f1s184ao f1mk8lai fnbmjn9 f1o700av f13mvf36 f1cmlufx f9n3di6 f1ids18y f1tx3yz7 f1deo86v f1eh06m1 f1iescvh fhgqx19 f1olyrje f1p93eir f1nev41a f1h8hb77 f1lqvz6u f10aw75t fsle3fq f17ae5zn" title="https://www.tum.de/en/news-and-events/all-news/press-releases/details/tum-recognized-as-university-of-excellence-for-the-fourth-consecutive-time" rel="noreferrer noopener">Technical University of Munich</a> has once again secured the prestigious designation as a University of Excellence. This marks TUM's fourth consecutive recognition in Germany’s most prestigious research and university funding competition, highlighting its outstanding achievements in research, teaching, innovation, and societal impact.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Awarded jointly by the German Research Foundation (DFG) and the German Council of Science and Humanities (Wissenschaftsrat), this honor recognizes universities whose strategic vision and research excellence set national standards. TUM has held this title without interruption since the program began in 2006, reaffirming its status as one of Germany’s most influential and innovative academic institutions.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>TUM School of Management contributes to TUM’s excellence mission</strong></p>
<p>At the TUM School of Management, research and teaching are deeply rooted in the intersection of management and technology. Through its interdisciplinary approach, the TUM School of Management plays a key role in advancing TUM’s mission to foster solution‑oriented research and develop talent capable of navigating the technological and societal transformations of the 21st century.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Participation in the Cluster of Excellence “TransforM”</strong></p>
<p>As part of the university’s excellence strategy, the TUM School of Management actively participates in the newly established Cluster of Excellence <a href="https://transform-cluster.de/" target="_blank" class="fui-Link ___1q1shib f2hkw1w f3rmtva f1ewtqcl fyind8e f1k6fduh f1w7gpdv fk6fouc fjoy568 figsok6 f1s184ao f1mk8lai fnbmjn9 f1o700av f13mvf36 f1cmlufx f9n3di6 f1ids18y f1tx3yz7 f1deo86v f1eh06m1 f1iescvh fhgqx19 f1olyrje f1p93eir f1nev41a f1h8hb77 f1lqvz6u f10aw75t fsle3fq f17ae5zn" title="https://transform-cluster.de/" rel="noreferrer noopener">“TransforM – the Munich Center for Transformative Technologies and Social Change.”</a></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>The cluster unites researchers from social sciences, engineering, natural sciences, and technology fields to explore how emerging technologies reshape organizations, markets, and society — and how these changes can be managed responsibly. With its expertise, the TUM School of Management contributes essential perspectives on the societal effects of technological change and enhances the cluster’s interdisciplinary approach.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>A commitment to excellence in the years ahead</strong></p>
<p>The renewed recognition as a University of Excellence motivates the TUM community — including the TUM School of Management — to continue striving for excellence in research, teaching, and societal engagement. With its interdisciplinary foundation and strong international focus, the School remains committed to advancing knowledge that tackles complex global challenges and promotes sustainable innovation.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2"> Climbing the Global Rankings in Entrepreneurship Research!</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>In the 2025 TCU Global University Entrepreneurship Research Productivity Rankings, TUM is listed among the Top 4 universities worldwide for research output in leading entrepreneurship journals.&nbsp;<br><br>This year’s result marks a jump from #7 to #4 within just one year, highlighting the growing influence of entrepreneurship research at <strong>TUM School of Management</strong>, and in particular, <strong>TUM Entrepreneurship Research Institute</strong>.&nbsp;<br>Congratulations, Oliver Alexy, Nicola Breugst, Hana Milanov, Holger Patzelt, Anne Tryba, Miriam Bird, Frank-Martin Belz, Claudia Doblinger, Hanna Hottenrott, Reiner Braun, Siddharth Vedula.&nbsp;<br><br>The ranking, compiled by the Texas Christian University - M.J. Neeley School of Business, evaluates publications in the field’s three top journals: Journal of Business Venturing (JBV), Entrepreneurship Theory and Practice (ETP), Strategic Entrepreneurship Journal (SEJ).<br><br>Using a clear methodology, one count per article, based on authors’ primary affiliation and without adjusting for faculty size,&nbsp;the ranking provides the only research-focused comparison of global entrepreneurship programs.<br><br>A strong recognition of TUM’s global<strong> </strong>impact and our commitment to advancing evidence-based entrepreneurship research.<br><br>➡️ To the ranking: <a href="https://www.neeley.tcu.edu/Academic-Departments/Entrepreneurship-and-Innovation/Global-Research-Rankings" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">www.neeley.tcu.edu/Academic-Departments/Entrepreneurship-and-Innovation/Global-Research-Rankings</a><br><br>&nbsp;</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Ann-Kristin Achleitner has been appointed to the newly established Investitions- und Innovationsbeirat</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>We are delighted to share that our Distinguished Affiliated Professor Ann-Kristin Achleitner has been appointed by Federal Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil to the newly established Investitions- und Innovationsbeirat (Advisory Council on Investment and Innovation).<br>This high-level council will advise the Minister on implementing and monitoring Germany’s unprecedented €500 billion investment package for infrastructure and climate neutrality.<br>Prof. Achleitner has been shaping the field of entrepreneurial finance for decades — she held the Chair of Entrepreneurial Finance at TUM School of Management from its establishment until 2020 and has been Scientific Co-Director of the Center for Entrepreneurial and Financial Studies, TU München since 2003.<br>Beyond academia, she brings extensive industry experience as a supervisory board member at several leading DAX companies.<br>With her expertise across academia, consulting, and industry, Prof. Achleitner will bring valuable insights to shaping Germany’s sustainable and innovative future.&nbsp;<br><br>&nbsp;We are proud she continues to contribute to TUM School of Management as Scientific Co-Director of CEFS and as a TUM Distinguished Affiliated Professor.&nbsp;</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Prof. Minner awarded the  2025 Science Award of the German Operations  Research Society</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>This highest honor of the GOR recognizes his outstanding contributions to <strong>Operations Research</strong>, especially in the field of stochastic inventory management. Prof. Minner is internationally recognized for advancing <strong>supplychain</strong> and <strong>logistics</strong> research through his highly cited publications and leadership in key academic associations. The award was presented during the opening ceremony of the OR 2025 conference in Bielefeld by Prof. Karl Inderfurth and Prof. Richard Hartl, which brought together hundreds of researchers and practitioners to discuss the future of Operations Research.</p>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Prof. Henkel appointed to the Expert Commission for Research and Innovation of the German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology, and Space</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>Congratulations to Prof. Dr. Joachim Henkel on his appointment to the Expert Commission for Research and Innovation (EFI - Expertenkommission Forschung und Innovation) of the German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology, and Space.</p>
<p>Since 2008, the EFI has provided independent scientific policy advice to the German government. Each year, the Commission publishes a report assessing Germany’s research, innovation, and technological performance in an international context and formulates recommendations for the future of innovation policy.</p>
<p>Prof. Dr. Henkel is Professor of Technology and Innovation Management at TUM School of Management. His research focuses on patent management, standards, technology acquisitions, digitalization, as well as open and user innovation.&nbsp;<br>With his expertise bridging science and economics, he will contribute to advancing Germany’s innovation landscape.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2"> Top Young Researcher 2025</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>Leonard Kinzinger has been recognized by BVM Berufsverband Deutscher Markt- und Sozialforscher e.V., VMÖ Verband der Marktforscher , SWISS INSIGHTS, Swiss Data Insights Association for the best Master’s thesis in market research in 2025.</p>
<p>His award-winning thesis, “Exploring the In-Context Learning Ability of LLMs to Create Realistic Synthetic Personalities,” investigates how granular microdata can be embedded into open-source large language models to simulate realistic consumer personas.</p>
<p>🎯 The goal: bridging the gap between #AI theory and practical application in market research.</p>
<p>While these AI-generated personas can’t fully replace real survey participants yet, Leonard’s work offers a scalable, fast, and insightful tool for exploring consumer behavior and societal trends.</p>
<p>Leonard is now pursuing his PhD in AI &amp; Music at the TUM Chair of Digital Marketing. He previously worked at Amazon as a BI Engineer and is currently co-authoring a paper under review at JAMS.</p>
<p>Congratulations on this outstanding achievement, Leonard! Your work sets a strong example of how AI can shape the future of market research.&nbsp;</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2"> A Remarkable Evening with Nobel Laureate Prof. Robert C. Merton</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>From past innovations to future visions, Prof. Merton captivated the audience with his profound insights into financial science.<br> <br> A recipient of the 1997 The Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for his groundbreaking work on the Black-Scholes-Merton model, he emphasized that true innovation arises from the coexistence of&nbsp; need, science, and technology.<br> <br> 🎤 “If you only look through the rear window while driving too fast, the road ahead may change before you realize it.”<br> <br> This powerful allegory underscored the rapid pace of financial evolution.<br> Prof. Merton also shared thought-provoking ideas on Retirement Security Bonds (RSBs) and the application of real options in infrastructure finance, highlighting striking examples such as Leipzig’s energy expansion in the 1990s.<br> <br> Before the main event, Prof. Merton took time to meet exclusively with 10 students, answering their questions and engaging in insightful discussions.<br> <br> A special highlight of the evening was when Prof. Merton presented the Deputy of the Dean, Professor Christoph Kaserer,&nbsp;and the with a unique gift:&nbsp; stationery from the hotel where Nobel Laureates stay in Stockholm, signed and kept for nearly 28 years.</p>
<p>This remarkable event was facilitated by Dimensional Fund Advisors in collaboration with the Technical University of Munich.<br> <br> A heartfelt thank you to Prof. Merton for an evening brimming with knowledge, inspiration, and history!</p></div>

<p>For 6 years in a row, we secured 1st place in management research in Germany and are the only German university in the world to rank among the top 150 management schools.</p>
<p>This accomplishment is a testament to the dedication of our academic community. The GRAS rankings recognize our excellence in World-Class Faculty, World-Class Output, High Quality Research, Research Impact and International Collaboration.</p>
<p>We're grateful for this recognition and committed to delivering exceptional academic work that shapes the future.</p>
<p>Since 2009, the Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU) by academic subject has been published annually by the Shanghai Ranking Consultancy. This release includes rankings of universities in 55 subjects from the fields of natural sciences, engineering, life sciences, medicine, and social sciences.</p>
<p>A total of more than 1,900 out of 5,000 universities from 96 countries and regions were included in the rankings.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Prestigious award for innovative paper</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>Great success for <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/in/miriam-bird-10b305159/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">Miriam Bird</a>, Professor of Entrepreneurship and Family Enterprise at the <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/tum-school-of-management/" target="_self">TUM School of Management</a> on the Campus Heilbronn, and her doctoral student Sidney Hribersek: The two researchers have been awarded the prestigious “FGF Norbert Szyperski Technology and Innovation Management Award 2024” for their innovative research article “Uncovering the Influence of CEO Curiosity on Eco-Innovations: Insights from German SMEs”.&nbsp;<br> <br> In their award-winning article, which Bird and Hribersek presented at the G-Forum in Ingolstadt at the end of September, they discuss the role of CEO curiosity in implementing eco-innovations in German Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs).&nbsp;<br> <br> One key finding: CEO curiosity is an important prerequisite for introducing eco-innovations.<br> <br> Based on the Upper Echelons Theory, according to which the characteristics and decisions of executives significantly influence corporate success, the authors conducted a large-scale survey among CEOs of German SMEs. The results show that the curiosity of CEOs is a decisive factor in introducing eco-innovations to reduce energy consumption and CO2 emissions. The study thus offers valuable practical insights for top management teams when selecting CEOs.<br> &nbsp;</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Congratulations to Rossella Rocchino for receiving the Best Scholarly Paper Award</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>We are delighted to share that TUM Doctoral Candidate and ATP scholarship recipient <strong>Rossella Rocchino</strong> and Prof. Christina Hertel from the University of Geneva have been awarded the Best Scholarly Paper Award at the 16th International Social Innovation Research Conference (ISIRC) 2024!&nbsp;</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Their research explores Community Entrepreneurship as a powerful avenue to foster meaningful impact in local communities.                                         <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Professor Farbmacher wins Best Paper Award</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>Congratulations to Professor Farbmacher for winning the Best Paper Award for his groundbreaking research on <em>"Linear Fixed-Effects Estimation with Nonrepeated Outcomes"</em> published in <em>Econometric Reviews</em>!</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>His work sheds light on biases in popular linear panel-data estimators, even when consistent with the linear model, and offers instrumental variable estimation as a promising alternative. An outstanding contribution to the field, supported by rigorous Monte Carlo simulations and empirical analysis. Well deserved!</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>The article, co-authored with Harald Tauchmann (FAU), was recognized with the Esfandiar Maasoumi Best Paper Award 2023, which honors the best paper in <em>Econometric Reviews</em> over a specific period. Farbmacher and Tauchmann’s research demonstrates that a statistical method frequently applied in empirical economics (linear fixed-effects estimation) can lead to systematically misleading results in certain cases and introduces a more robust alternative. The award-winning paper is available as an Open Access article for a limited time: <a href="https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/07474938.2023.2224658" target="_new" rel="noreferrer">https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/07474938.2023.2224658</a>.</p></div>

                                    <div class="text-content relative pl-8 pt-8 pb-6 pr-6 h-[356px] md:h-[320px] overflow-hidden transition-all duration-500 ease-in-out">
                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2"> Congratulations to Mahsa Nakhost for receiving the ISIR Best Student Paper Award 2024</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>Congratulations to Mahsa Abbaszadeh Nakhost, research assistant at the TUM Chair of Logistics and Supply Chain Management, who received the ISIR Best Student Paper Award for her paper &nbsp;"Inventory Transshipment for Promotional Products with Non-Stationary Demand and Updating," co-authored by Gudrun Kiesmüller and Stefan Minner.&nbsp;</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>The paper addresses the challenges of inventory transshipment for promotional products in the retail industry. The study introduces a novel approach using Bayesian methodology and a non-homogeneous Poisson Process to balance the trade-off between delaying transshipment for more information and acting early to maximize sales.</p>
<p>The research demonstrates significant profit improvements by accurately modeling demand and optimizing transshipment timing.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>The award was presented at the 22nd International Symposium on Inventories in Budapest by the International Society for Inventory Research.</p>
<p>Congratulations to Mahsa for this remarkable achievement! We are incredibly proud to have outstanding students like her who are internationally recognized for their excellence.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Our winners of the Social Impact Award 2024</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>The winners of the Social Impact Award 2024 were announced at this year's TUM Entrepreneurship Day.<br> <br> Students, graduates, and alumni of the TUM School of Management were eligible to participate in the Social Impact Award and win up to €2,000 for their innovative approach to solving a social problem.<br> <br> 🏆 The first place goes to Samuel Keitel, Tim Findeiss, and Staël Wilfried Tchinda Kuete for Senior Connect, which matches senior professionals with companies, ensuring mutual benefit: companies gain from the vast experience and wisdom of seniors while seniors engage in meaningful employment, enhancing their quality of life and financial independence.<br> <br> 🥈 2nd place winner: Lisa Christin Zimmermann and Philipp Middendorf with Student consultancy La Paz, Bolivia<br> As part of their project study at the TUM Chair for Strategy and Organization under the supervision of Professor Isabell Welpe, they have now set the goal of establishing the concept of student consultancy in Bolivia, thereby creating social and economic value. This project presents an ideal opportunity to contribute to promoting education in developing countries, assuming responsibility, and gaining entrepreneurial experience.<br> <br> 🥉 3rd place winner: Sebastian Moosheimer with workride.<br> Workride is a digital platform that links corporations and their commuting employees with shuttle operators and drivers. Utilizing route algorithms developed in close collaboration with two TUM institutes, the platform pools in commuters from various companies. They use employee data and AI-based route generation to identify the most popular routes to predict shuttle service demand.<br> <br> The award is sponsored by our wonderful <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/in/tum-management-alumni-e-v-137101149/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">TUM Management Alumni e.V.</a><br> The judges of the Social Impact Awards 2024 were Professor Siddharth Vedula (Chair of Entrepreneurship and Communities), Professor Claudia Doblinger (Chair of Innovation and Technology Management), and Professor Frank-Martin Belz (Chair of Entrepreneurial Sustainability).<br> <br> 👏 We are proud to see that all three projects have successfully addressed a social issue and positively impacted society. 👏 Congratulations!</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">First ERC Grant for TUM Campus Heilbronn</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>Excellent news and a great honor for Prof. Dr. <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/in/ACoAAAqLnvYBYfXNH74EI9LUGXGa9eV9spZYdr4" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">Jens Foerderer</a>, Professor for Innovation and Digitalization at the <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/tum-campus-heilbronn/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">TUM Campus Heilbronn</a>: The ambitious professor will be funded by the <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/european-research-council/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">European Research Council (ERC)</a> with a total of 1.5 million euros over the next five years.&nbsp;</p>
<p>His research project "Fair Competition in App Markets" convinced the ERC committee. His pioneering research aims to understand how Apple's and Google's obligations under the European Union's Digital Markets Directive affect competition and innovation in their app stores.&nbsp;</p>
<p>With this prestigious funding, Prof. Förderer will advance his research goals in a targeted and focused manner. He has a clear vision: "Digital markets play an immensely important role in the global economy, but are controlled by a few platforms. We need to better understand how to ensure competition, innovation and fairness in digital markets.</p>
<p>The grant approval is an important milestone in this journey, as research is costly and the funds can be used to establish an academic working group for the winning project. In addition, many research projects were competing for these important resources. Jens Förderer is therefore happy and proud of the Research Council's decision: "This funding is an award that very few researchers receive. I am overjoyed that my research convinced the Commission and the reviewers.</p></div>

The Academy of Management was founded in 1936 and has about 20,000 members, comprising management and economics scholars from around the world.</p>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Professor Horst Wildemann received the honorary doctorate from the Hamburg University of Technology (TUHH)</p>

Horst Wildemann&nbsp;received the honorary doctorate from the&nbsp;Hamburg University of Technology&nbsp;(TUHH), which was presented to him by TUHH President Prof.&nbsp;Andreas Timm-Giel&nbsp;and TUHH Vice President&nbsp;Wolfgang Kersten.&nbsp;<br> <br> Professor Wildemann was honored for successfully linking science and operational practice, for reducing the&nbsp;vaccine&nbsp;shortage during the COVID-19 epidemic, and for his services to the international competitiveness of the German&nbsp;automotive&nbsp;industry.<br> <br> Professor Wildemann developed a modular production system called "BioNTainer" for the COVID-19 vaccine manufacturer&nbsp;BioNTech SE. This enabled the Mainz-based pharmaceutical company to scale up the production of its Covid-19 vaccine during the pandemic.<br> <br> “I would like to extend my sincere congratulations to Professor Wildemann on his well-deserved honorary doctorate. This is an amazing achievement that highlights his dedication and exceptional contributions to science and the industry. Congratulations on this tremendous achievement!”, said Professor&nbsp;Gunther Friedl, Dean of the&nbsp;TUM School of Management.<br> <br> Professor Horst Wildemann held the Chair of Business Administration, Corporate Management, Logistics, and Production at the&nbsp;Technical University of Munich, and has headed the Munich-based consultancy&nbsp;TCW Management Consulting&nbsp;for more than 30 years now. Wildeman is also the initiator of the conference&nbsp;Münchner Management Kolloquium, which is held annually at TUM.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Mentor of Excellence Award goes to Professor Isabell Welpe</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>At the TUM Entrepreneurship Day, Isabell Welpe, Professor of TUM Chair for Strategy and Organization, was honored with the TUM Start-up Mentor of Excellence Award.</p>
<p>With this award, the TUM honors professors who are particularly committed and successful in mentoring #startup teams. Many scientists accompany the teams during the application and the one-year term of an EXIST start-up grant. Mentoring by scientists is a prerequisite for receiving one of the coveted federal grants for university spin-offs.<br> &nbsp;<br> Professor Welpe´s research focuses on the digital transformation of companies, business model innovations, the impact of digital technologies on businesses and organizations, and the future of leadership and work/organizational design.<br> She studied Management at the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München and at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Boston, USA. She also completed an MSc at the London School of Economics.</p>
<p>She is a research fellow at University College London. Isabell Welpe teaches strategy and business model innovation, digital transformation, leadership, organizational design, and managing people and organizations. Her research has been reported in the media, e.g. Harvard Business Manager and MIT Sloan Management Review.</p>
<p>We congratulate Professor Welpe on this fantastic achievement!</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Professor Gudrun Kiesmüller receives honorary doctorate from Otto-von-Guericke-Universität Magdeburg University</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>Professor Gudrun Kiesmüller receives honorary doctorate from Otto-von-Guericke-Universität Magdeburg University,&nbsp;which was presented to her by the dean of the faculty of Economics and Management Prof. Dr. Abdolkarim Sadrieh (left) and the rector of the university Prof. Dr. Jens Strackeljan (right).</p>
<p>The renowned professor receives this award for her outstanding scientific achievements, particularly in connection with the optimal planning and design of supply chains, manufacturing systems and maintenance processes.</p>
<p>With numerous publications in internationally renowned journals, Prof. Kiesmüller is one of Germany's leading researchers in business administration. Her expertise spans various areas of production and logistics research, especially in supply chain management and inventory management.</p>
<p>Furthermore, prior to her move to TUM in 2019, Prof. Kiesmüller was instrumental in founding the research cluster "Center of Operations Research and Business Analytics" (CORBA) at the University of Magdeburg and developed the successful master program "Operations Research and Business Analytics". Her dedicated work and commitment have contributed to the redesign of the Master's programs at the Faculty of Economics and Management, thus significantly influencing the study landscape of business administration at the University of Magdeburg.</p>
<p>“I would like to extend my sincere congratulations to Professor Kiesmüller on her well-deserved honorary doctorate. This is an amazing achievement that highlights her dedication, hard work, and exceptional contributions to science and academia. Her expertise, enthusiasm and dedication are an inspiration to us all. I am very grateful to have Professor Kiesmüller at the TUM School of Management. She was the first TUM professor at our TUM Campus Heilbronn and significantly contributed to our growth. Congratulations on this tremendous achievement!”, said Professor Gunther Friedl, Dean of the TUM School of Management.</p>

                                    <div class="text-content relative pl-8 pt-8 pb-6 pr-6 h-[356px] md:h-[320px] overflow-hidden transition-all duration-500 ease-in-out">
                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">OpenAI Founder Visits Munich</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>Rarely has a technology sparked such intense discussion as ChatGPT, the artificial intelligence (AI)-based chatbot. The brain behind it and co-founder of OpenAI, Sam Altman, visited TUM on May 25th, 2023. In the Audimax, he explained the reasons for its success, why ChatGPT is not an open source technology, and how it could be regulated.</p>
<p>After less than half an hour, the 1,100-seat Audimax was sold out for the 38-year-old's only public event in Germany during his European tour. Under questioning from Reinhard Heckel, professor of machine learning, Sam Altman, along with OpenAI developer Johannes Heidecke, recounted the evolution of the language model to its current fourth version. "Even with GPT-3, the whole company wasn't convinced," Altman said. The key to its success, he said, is its natural language chat capability, which provides an even better human-computer interface than the touchscreen. However, ChatGPT is still misunderstood as a large database, he said.</p>
<p>Altman explained why OpenAI made the technology available to the public early on, following a "show, don't tell" approach: "We feel strongly that we should educate the world about it and give people time to gradually adapt to the technology”. That way, he said, there can be a discussion about how to deal with artificial intelligence. This, he said, is better than keeping technologies secret in the lab for a long time because it would supposedly scare people into releasing them too soon.</p>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">CHE University Ranking 2023: Students give TUM School of Management top ratings</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>TUM School of Management students from&nbsp;Heilbronn&nbsp;and&nbsp;Munich&nbsp;are highly satisfied with the teaching standards and study conditions in their management studies.<br> <br> In the new ranking by the&nbsp;<a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/che-centre-for-higher-education/" target="_blank" data-attribute-index="2" data-entity-type="MINI_COMPANY" rel="noreferrer">CHE Centre for Higher Education</a>, they give their school the highest marks. The TUM School of Management receives top ratings in its subject. Students are particularly satisfied with the general study situation and digital teaching. Especially the&nbsp;<a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/tum-campus-heilbronn/" target="_blank" data-attribute-index="4" data-entity-type="MINI_COMPANY" rel="noreferrer">TUM Campus Heilbronn</a>&nbsp;receives five stars for its rooms and equipment on its modern campus.<br> <br> In research, the School scores the highest marks in research reputation and is also in the top group in terms of&nbsp; research funding per scientist as well as doctorates and&nbsp; publications per professor.<br> The subject ranking also awards our faculty in&nbsp;Straubing&nbsp;a high research reputation and they also achieve top group rankings for research funding per scientist and doctorates per professor. Students in Straubing were not able to participate in the survey yet.<br> Overall, TUM School of Management was able to improve its ratings compared to the results from the last evaluation two years ago and received above-average ratings for all of the categories assessed by the survey.</p>
<p>Germany's largest university ranking - facts and opinions from 120,000 students and 3,000 professors. The CHE compares individual subjects at German-speaking universities, this time in business administration/management. The ranking is primarily intended to provide orientation for prospective students. The focus is on the opinion of around 120,000 students surveyed. The universities are rated in numerous categories on a scale from one to five stars.</p>
<p>In their management programs overall, TUM receives at least four stars in all categories. For the "general study situation," students award four and a half stars. The same top ratings were given for the range of courses offered, the support provided by the lecturers and the organization of the studies. Especially at the Heilbronn Campus, TUM even receives five stars for their rooms and equipment on its modern campus.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>The CHE rating proves once again, that the TUM School of Management delivers excellent research and teaching. The students value the study opportunities and variety of courses, which is reflected also in the extracurricular opportunities offered by the TUM ecosystem.<br> &nbsp;</p>

                                    <div class="text-content relative pl-8 pt-8 pb-6 pr-6 h-[356px] md:h-[320px] overflow-hidden transition-all duration-500 ease-in-out">
                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Top rankings for educating “Digital Leaders”</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p><strong>TUM School of Management is the number one in the world to educate students in digitalization and worldwide third for training digital start-up leaders</strong></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>In the latest edition of the Digital Leaders in Higher Education – a series of the Global Ranking for Best Universities for Digital Learning and Studies – TUM School of Management&nbsp; has earned first place.&nbsp;</p>
<p>Which universities train their students best to work with digital technologies? Who is producing the future "digital leaders" in large companies and in startups?</p>
<p>To find out, consulting firms Emerging and Trendence used the Crunchbase database to identify the university degrees of 110,000 digital professionals at the world's most innovative companies. They also asked around 3,600 IT professionals, startup founders and young professionals which universities they would recruit graduates from. The result is the "Global Ranking for Best Universities for Digital Learning and Studies" in the "Digital Leaders in Higher Education" series.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Here’s what they found out:</strong></p>
<p>- TUM with its School of Management is the world's best university in "Digital companies' management studies". In this category, the ranking evaluates how many managers of digital companies have studied business, marketing and/or finance at the respective universities.</p>
<p>- TUM also ranks third after the University of Tokyo and the University of Melbourne in terms of training for digital startups. For this category, the degrees of the founders were evaluated and the digital experts were asked about the best entrepreneurship programs.</p>
<p>- In the overall ranking, TUM achieved 11th place, which means that it has improved by seven places compared to the previous year.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Especially at TUM Campus Heilbronn we educate digital thinkers, future leaders, entrepreneurs, and pioneers. Hereby, we are as technology-driven as their careers ahead. Our interdisciplinary approach in the study programs combining management and technology prepares our students to shape the future. At Campus Heilbronn the TUM School of Management offers the Bachelor in Management &amp; Technology as well as the <a href="/programs/master-in-management/heilbronn">Master in Management </a>to educate digital leaders.</p>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">New TUM AI Task Force established</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>The TUM Think Tank is setting up a task force to provide orientation and guidance on handling generative artificial intelligence to the policy, administration, community and business sectors. The group, representing various disciplines at the Technical University of Munich (TUM), will formulate regulatory proposals and will facilitate exchange on practical questions.</p>
<p>The members of the <a href="https://www.tum.de/en/news-and-events/all-news/press-releases/details/neue-task-force-zu-generativer-ki" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">Generative AI Task Force</a> contribute expertise from a wide variety of perspectives in research on technologies, social sciences, ethics as well as several application areas. These include education, administration, justice, business and health.&nbsp;</p>
<p><a href="https://www.professoren.tum.de/en/welpe-isabell-m" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">Prof. Isabell Welpe</a> is one of the founding members representing the School of Management.&nbsp;Her research focuses on the digital transformation of companies, business model innovations, the impact of digital technologies on business and organizations, and the future of leadership and work/organizational design.</p>

                                        <div class="content"><p>Diapers, band-aids, canned food, and sleeping bags are among the most needed items that our student council collects for the victims of the devastating&nbsp;<a href="https://www.linkedin.com/feed/hashtag/?keywords=earthquake&amp;highlightedUpdateUrns=urn%3Ali%3Aactivity%3A7031999841111035904" target="_blank" data-attribute-index="0" rel="noreferrer">earthquake</a>&nbsp;in Turkey and Syria.<br> <br> “Our Turkish fellow students approached us and we set up the&nbsp;donation&nbsp;campaign within 4 days,” say Adrian, Estefania, and Uttam from the&nbsp;<a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/student-council-tum-school-of-management/" target="_blank" data-attribute-index="2" data-entity-type="MINI_COMPANY" rel="noreferrer">Student Council TUM School of Management</a>. The donations will be picked up by the Turkish General Consulate in Munich and transported directly to the affected regions.<br> <br> Our dean Professor&nbsp;Gunther Friedl&nbsp;visited the TUM students today: “I was shocked to hear about the tragic earthquake in Turkey and Syria. Our heartfelt condolences and thoughts go out to all of the victims and their families. The&nbsp;Technical University of Munich&nbsp;has provided the necessary infrastructure.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Congratulations to Professor Siddharth Vedula for winning the Supervisory Award! </p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>Congratulations to Professor Siddharth Vedula for winning the Supervisory Award!&nbsp;<br> Prof. Vedula (left) won the award for his great support and dedication to his doctoral students. His students are working on several interesting topics at his chair including the study of corporate accelerators, renewable energy innovation, and the “dark side” of entrepreneurship.</p>
<p>His students praise him for his great support in developing research projects, while at the same time showing very good leadership skills. Professor Vedula ensures his doctoral students make continuous progress in their research and studies, while also being a mentor and role model to them.</p>
<p>Sid Vedula is a professor at the TUM Entrepreneurship Research Institute. His research interests include the geography of entrepreneurship and environmental entrepreneurship.&nbsp;</p>
<p>He has studied a wide range of topics, including spatial contagion behavior in the venture capital investment industry, regional differences in the adoption of green building practices, how ideological differences in communities shape renewable energy entrepreneurship, and the dynamics of regional entrepreneurial ecosystems.</p>
<p>Our Dean Prof. Gunther Friedl presented the award to Prof. Vedula in the name of the doctoral students. We are very proud to have such an outstanding and dedicated member of our faculty!&nbsp;</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">New collaboration with Beedie School of Business at Simon Fraser University, British Columbia in Canada</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>The TUM School of Management recently developed a strategic #partnership with the Beedie School of Business Simon Fraser University. The agreement is a Letter of Intent to develop a strategic partnership between both business schools.</p>
<p>Our Assoc. Dean for International Alliances Professor Thomas Hutzschenreuter traveled to Canada to meet with the Dean of Beedie School of Business Professor Ujwal Kayande.</p>
<p>We share a common interest in many academic and educational fields; and in order to promote future institutional cooperation, we signed a Letter of Intent and agreed to develop and carry out collaborative activities, such as: exchange of scholarly publications and information; exchange of faculty, staff, and students, development of collaborative research projects and programs.</p>
<p>We are delighted to start the new collaboration with the Beedie School of Business and are looking forward to many insightful exchanges with our colleagues and friends from British Colombia!</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Forbes Magazine - Power To The Student: Inspiring The Next Generation Of Leaders At The MBA World Summit</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>Studying business is popular – really popular. The MBA has been the number one graduate degree in the U.S. for over a decade, and the OECD - OCDE estimates that roughly 25% of higher education students around the world are studying in the field of business. From management and marketing to finance and analytics, business graduates are everywhere.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>So business schools have a huge responsibility. After all, they are shaping the behaviours of those who will be leading many of our institutions and businesses of the future. As the world faces growing societal, economic and environmental issues, we need leaders to be well informed and aligned to tackle these problems effectively and appropriately.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Matt Symonds captures the energy and ideas of the MBA World Summit for Forbes, and the importance of human connection. As the Dean of TUM School of Management,<strong> </strong><strong>Gunther Friedl advises, "Choose your circle wisely."</strong></p>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">TUM School of Management takes the lead as strongest research university </p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>The German business magazine&nbsp;<a href="https://www.wiwo.de/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer"><em>WirtschaftsWoche</em></a> published a new ranking on the number of research publications issued by researchers in the area of business and management currently employed at universities in the German-speaking countries. Our research focuses on future trends and real-world solutions that advance innovation-based businesses and benefit society at large. Students benefit from the use of cutting edge research in the classroom. </u></p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Professor of the Year Award 2022 for Chengguang Li</p>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Congratulations to Professor Paul P. Momtaz for winning a WAIFC Young Academic Award 2022 </p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>Congratulations&nbsp;to Professor&nbsp;Paul P. Momtaz&nbsp;for winning a WAIFC Young Academic Award 2022 for his paper on Financing Sustainable Entrepreneurship: ESG Measurement, Valuation, and Performance in Token Offerings which was recently published in the&nbsp;Journal of Business Venturing.<br> <br> The award was presented in Casablanca at the Sustainable Finance Dialogue, a joint initiative between the&nbsp;World Alliance of International Financial Centers (WAIFC)&nbsp;and the&nbsp;UNDP Financial Centres for Sustainability (FC4S)&nbsp;network, the green finance initiative led by the&nbsp;United Nations&nbsp;Development Program (UN DP).<br> &nbsp;<br> Professor Momtaz joined the Professorship of Entrepreneurial Finance at TUM SoM just recently. His paper looks at sustainable Entrepreneurship (SE), which seeks to attain profitability and sustainability goals.<br> <br> A major research gap concerns the economic attractiveness of SE for entrepreneurs and investors. The question is ambiguous because sustainability orientation creates costly constraints, while startups cannot fully appropriate their positive externalities. Paul Momtaz and co-author Sasan Mansouri relate startups’ Environment, Society, and Governance (ESG) properties obtained from a machine-learning approach (<a href="https://lnkd.in/eiJv_4ti" target="_blank" data-attribute-index="14" rel="noreferrer">https://lnkd.in/eiJv_4ti</a>) to SE valuation and performance in token offerings.<br> <br> Startups with salient ESG goals are able to raise financing at more favorable valuations, incentivizing entrepreneurs to adopt ESG goals in the first place. However, their post-funding performance is weaker than in conventional startups, suggesting that investors incur a relative financial loss for backing sustainability-oriented entrepreneurs.<br> <br> ➡️Download the paper:&nbsp;<a href="https://lnkd.in/ectuHchS" target="_blank" data-attribute-index="15" rel="noreferrer">https://lnkd.in/ectuHchS</a><br> &nbsp;<br> The WAIFC facilitates cooperation between financial centers, the exchange of best practices, and communication with the general public.</p></div>

                                    <div class="text-content relative pl-8 pt-8 pb-6 pr-6 h-[356px] md:h-[320px] overflow-hidden transition-all duration-500 ease-in-out">
                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Young researchers discuss the latest developments in Deep Reinforcement Learning</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>About 30 international professors and young researchers discussed the latest developments in Deep Reinforcement Learning for dynamic decision problems in logistics and healthcare in a 3-day workshop at our TUM Campus Heilbronn.</p>
<p>The workshop was organized by professors Gudrun Kiesmüller, Jingui Xie and Stefan Minner and included presentations and interactive sessions, such as a research pitch and a coding challenge.</p>
<p>“As a PhD student, I presented my research project and received a lot of valuable feedback. I also discussed my working paper with two experienced researchers, which was a great exchange of ideas and I could learn from their detailed suggestions,” said Yihua Wang.</p>
<p>The workshop focused on applying Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to decision-making problems in inventory management, transportation, production, auction games, and healthcare. Due to the 𝘂𝗻𝗶𝗾𝘂𝗲 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗰𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘀𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺𝘀, it is challenging to adapt reinforcement learning to efficiently solve real-world problems. Typically, the problems are high-dimensional and have large uncertainties, which complicates the learning process.</p>
<p>“I massively enjoyed the workshop, and the presentations by senior faculty and Ph.D. students were truly thought-provoking. For example, I counted four ingenious and generalizable ideas for dealing with large action spaces: Ideas that will contribute to further adoption of DRL in practical contexts. It was great catching up with collaborators on the subject, but it was perhaps even more valuable to connect with so many new people who bring exciting new ideas to the area.“ says Prof. Willem van Jaarsveld of Eindhoven University of Technology.</p>
<p>Key learnings include:</p>
<p>Some real-world problems can be solved better with smart other heuristics instead of applying DRL</p>
<p>New promising ideas have been developed to solve problems with DRL and large action spaces</p>
<p>Good domain knowledge is needed to solve real-world problems with DRL</p>
<p>Thank you to all participants for your great contributions!</p>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">BMW CEO Oliver Zipse appointed TUM Honorary Professor</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>The Chairman of the Board of Management of BMW AG <strong>Oliver Zipse </strong>was appointed honorary professor at the Technical University of Munich (TUM) today. Zipse has been teaching courses on the transformation of the automotive industry at the TUM School of Management since 2019.</p>
<p>The "CEO Pitch" is the highlight of the seminar "Innovative Automotive Production and Current Transformation Fields", which Oliver Zipse has been holding at the TUM School of Management since 2019. Here, the BMW CEO not only teaches the theoretical basics of global markets, production systems and digital innovations. The students also develop their own analyses and strategies for current challenges in the industry in exchange with various departments of the company. The course regularly receives excellent ratings in student evaluations.</p>
<p>"Hardly any other sector is as crucial for Germany as the automotive industry is for the country as a business location. That's why the importance of its transformation extends far beyond the industry itself," emphasizes Prof. Gunther Friedl, Dean of the TUM School of Management. "This makes it all the more important that we train students who not only know the theory, but also the corporate world. No lecture, no matter how good, can replace teamwork on real issues."</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">The winners of the TUM Business Game 2022</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>Two and half days of hard work paid off for our winning team of the <a href="https://tum-businessgame.com/" target="_blank" title="TUM Business Game" rel="noreferrer">TUM Business Game</a> 2022. Congratulations to our students:<br> &nbsp;<br> ● &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;Ceren Sensoy | TUM M.Sc. Management &amp; Technology<br> ● &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;Sanchit Nevatia | TUM M.Sc. Management&nbsp;<br> ● &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;Niels Nielsen | TUM M.Sc. Sustainable Management &amp; Technology<br> ● &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;Kirill Molchanov | TUM B.Sc. Management &amp; Technology<br> &nbsp;<br> This year, 60 students were preselected out of a pool of 400 applicants for the TUM Business Game, the biggest case study competition in Munich. In different teams, they faced real-world business challenges designed by top-class partners Microsoft, SAP, Accenture and Siemens. With the help of the industry partners, the teams had to solve cases that included the development of a profitability analysis for a vertical farming project and a concept for a new modern way of working remotely.<br> &nbsp;<br> The winning team found it challenging to blend the ideas of all members into one solution that everybody could agree on. But for Kirill Molchanov, the diversity of the team turned out to be a decisive factor: “Each team member came from a different background and hence brought with them a different skill set that helped us to analyze the case study in a multidimensional way.” Ceren Sensoy is convinced that the skills that they developed at TUM School Management were crucial to their victory: “We were able to win this game because TUM School of Management equipped us with skills we acquired in courses such as Finance, Strategy, Marketing, and Entrepreneurship.”<br> &nbsp;<br> <strong>A lively exchange between students and industry partners</strong><br> &nbsp;<br> In between solving the cases, all participants had the opportunity to connect with like-minded students as well as industry experts. A chance that winner Sanchit Nevatia did not want to miss out on: “The combination of analyzing interesting business case studies and broadening my professional network intrigued me and made me want to participate.”<br> &nbsp;<br> By taking part in the TUM Business Game, the project partners can find potential employees who meet their high standards. “TUM students fit perfectly into our world because they combine strategy and technology,” said Angelika Kasperek from Accenture. Dominik Gursch from Microsoft added that the fresh ideas from TUM students help the company gain a deeper understanding of their projects.<br> &nbsp;<br> Naturally, the project partners also wanted to return this favor and create added value beyond the actual competition. Thus, they gave students insights into their day-to-day experiences and discussed current developments in their respective industries. Winner Niels Nielsen learned a lot during the event: “The TUM Business Game was a great opportunity to see what topics the four companies are working on and to make many exciting contacts.”<br> &nbsp;<br> <strong>TUM Business Game - Building the bridge between companies and academia</strong><br> &nbsp;<br> The TUM Business Game is the biggest case study competition in Munich. Since 2016, it has been organized by students for students. Finding solutions for current challenges prepares them for developing successful business concepts in the future. Even though the cases are taken out of real-life situations, the students can make mistakes - in the end, the TUM Business Game is just a game. With this safety in mind, they are encouraged to experiment and find innovative and out-of-the-box solutions. The event gives students the opportunity to make themselves known to potential employers. Vice versa, our top-class partners can find potential employees that fit their expectations perfectly.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Shanghai Ranking of Academic Subjects: Top German Management School</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p><strong>TUM School of Management was once again ranked</strong><strong>&nbsp;among the</strong><strong>&nbsp;top</strong><strong>&nbsp;Business Schools&nbsp;</strong><strong>in the latest&nbsp;Global Ranking of Academic Subjects (GRAS) 2022&nbsp;released today. TUM School of Management secured No. 1 for&nbsp;</strong><strong><a href="http://www.shanghairanking.com/rankings/gras/2021" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">management research</a></strong><strong>&nbsp;in Germany five years in a row now. Worldwide, TUM School of Management ranks as the only German school among the Top 150 Management Schools.</strong></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Since 2009, the Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU) by academic subjects has been published annually by the Shanghai Ranking Consultancy. This release contains rankings of universities in 54 subjects across Natural Sciences, Engineering, Life Sciences, Medical Sciences, and Social Sciences. In total, more than 1,800 out of 4,000 universities across 93 countries and regions were listed in the rankings. Universities are ranked by several indicators of academic or research performance. The GRAS rankings use a range of academic indicators and third-party data to measure the performance of world universities in respective subjects, including research output, research influence, international collaboration, research quality, and international academic awards.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">QS Ranking 2023: TUM ranked number 1 German university for the eighth time in a row</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>In the latest edition of the respected <a href="https://www.topuniversities.com/university-rankings/world-university-rankings/2023" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">QS World University Ranking</a>, the Technical University of Munich (TUM) is ranked number one among German universities for the eighth time in succession. It is also number three in the European Union and is ranked among the top 50 universities in the world.</p>
<p>The British university service provider QS Quacquarelli Symonds compiles its university quality rankings through surveys of academics and employers. It also assesses the number of citations of published research, the faculty-student ratio and the percentages of international students and staff.<br> <br> TUM moved up to 49th place worldwide and is thus yet again the top-ranked German university – followed by LMU on rank 59. Within the EU TUM is the third best university, behind Université PSL and Institut Polytechnique, both from Paris.</p>
<p><strong>19th overall in engineering</strong></p>
<p>In the most recent issue of the QS World University Rankings by Subject, in which QS ranks universities by subject areas and individual disciplines, TUM placed 19th in engineering and 28th in natural sciences. In five individual disciplines it scored top-25 rankings, including 16th in physics/astronomy and 18th in electrical engineering.<br> <br> TUM also regularly achieves excellent results in other international rankings. For example, it holds the 38th position in the THE World University Ranking and is number 12 worldwide in the Global University Employability Ranking, in which companies rate the quality of graduates.</p></div>

                                    <div class="text-content relative pl-8 pt-8 pb-6 pr-6 h-[356px] md:h-[320px] overflow-hidden transition-all duration-500 ease-in-out">
                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Professor of behavioral research methods joins  TUM School of Management</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p><strong>Joining us for his new appointment at TUM School of Management in Munich is Prof. Dr. Thorsten Pachur, Professor of Behavioral Research Methods. His research and areas of interest lie in the fields of adaptive cognition, decision-making, cognitive modeling, and process tracing. With such a rich depth and breadth of knowledge, we could not be more pleased to have him further enrich our already outstanding team of educators. We are delighted to welcome Prof. Pachur, and we wish him a successful start at TUM!</strong></p>
<p>April 1, 2022. Joining us for his new appointment at TUM School of Management in Munich is Prof. Dr. Thorsten Pachur, Professor of Behavioral Research Methods. His research investigates adaptive cognition, that is, how the psychological mechanisms underlying thinking, reasoning and decision-making are shaped by the structure of the environment. A key idea is that successful decision-making can arise from the intelligent use of simple strategies – heuristics - that exploit regularities in the environment. Dr. Pachur’s research covers decision-making under risk and judgment, under uncertainty, and he is also interested in the role of intuition, and how decision-making develops across the lifespan. In his research, Dr. Pachur employs an integrative multi-method approach that includes behavioral experiments, computational modeling, process tracing (e.g., eye tracking), and neuroimaging.</p>
<p>Thorsten Pachur studied psychology at the Free University Berlin and the University of Sussex. He obtained his PhD in psychology from the Free University Berlin in 2006 and his habilitation from the University of Basel in 2012. He has worked as a research scientist at the University of Basel (2006-2012) and as a senior research scientist at the Max Planck Institute for Human Development (2012-2022).</p>
<p>Congratulations on your new appointment and best of luck in your future endeavors here at the TUM School of Management!</p></div>
