                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Welcome Prof. Dr. Melanie Richards</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>March 1, 2022. Joining us for her new appointment at TUM School of Management in Munich is Prof. Dr.&nbsp;<a href="/faculty-research/academic-departments/innovation-entrepreneurship" target="_blank">Melanie Richards</a>, Professor of Family Business Culture and Ownership. Her research focuses on how family firms’ unique culture affects organisational decision-making and outcomes. Moreover, Melanie Richards’ work seeks to better understand the entrepreneurial and social activities of business families. Thereby her research investigates the families’ financial and non-financial goals, their values and socio-emotional wealth. Her research also analyses family philanthropy and impact investing, which constitute important practical phenomena, yet remain under-theorized in academia. With such a rich depth and breadth of knowledge, we could not be more pleased to have her further enrich our already outstanding team of educators. We are delighted to welcome Prof. Richards, and we wish her a successful start at TUM!</p>
<p>Prof. Dr. Richards is joining the&nbsp;<a href="/faculty-research/academic-departments/innovation-entrepreneurship" target="_blank">Department of Innovation &amp; Entrepreneurship</a>&nbsp;as Professor of Family Business Culture &amp; Ownership. Prior to joining the TUM School of Management, Melanie Richards was Associate Professor in Entrepreneurship and Innovation at the University of Bath. She also worked for the University of Bristol as Assistant Professor in Management and for the University of St. Gallen as Postdoctoral Researcher at the Center for Family Business after receiving her PhD in Management from the University of St. Gallen in September 2015. As part of her PhD education she spent 12 months as Visiting Scholar at Bayes Business School in London. Prior to her academic career, Melanie Richards gained experience as a consultant working for PwC Management-Consulting in London.</p>
<p>Congratulations on your new appointment and best of luck in your future endeavors here at the TUM School of Management!</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Insights from virtual reality-enhanced teaching at TUM Campus Heilbronn</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>Virtual Reality (VR) has great potential, which is still vastly untapped in management education. The COVID-19 pandemic forced us to teach remotely and search for meaningful alternatives to online video communication tools. The team of Prof. Dr.&nbsp;<a href="https://www.wi.tum.de/tum-campus-heilbronn/center-for-digital-transformation/prof-dr-wuttke/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">David Wuttke</a>, Assistant Professor for Supply Chain Management of TUM School of Management at&nbsp;<a href="https://www.wi.tum.de/tum-campus-heilbronn/welcome-tum-campus-heilbronn/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">TUM Campus Heilbronn</a>&nbsp;explored the use of a virtual classroom environment in two courses in the summer term of 2021. In the solution, students and faculty were represented by avatars and communicated in a digital representation of a real classroom.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.wi.tum.de/wp-content/uploads/2016/09/White-Paper-Teaching-in-VR_TUM_2022.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">The white paper is available for download here.</a></p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Algorithms do not have a vision</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p><a href="https://www.professoren.tum.de/en/hutzschenreuter-thomas" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Professor Thomas Hutzschenreuter</a>&nbsp;discusses the usability of AI for managerial decision-making in an article of the FAZ. Algorithms are extremely useful for frequent and stable decision situations such as purchasing, logistics’ as well as maintenance decisions, but fail in infrequent and unstable situations. For rare and unique entrepreneurial decisions a human entrepreneurial decision-maker is still needed and cannot be substituted by AI.&nbsp;<a href="https://www.faz.net/aktuell/wirtschaft/kuenstliche-intelligenz-kann-fuer-firmen-tueckisch-sein-17784020.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Read on here</a>.</p></div>

                                    <div class="text-content relative pl-8 pt-8 pb-6 pr-6 h-[356px] md:h-[320px] overflow-hidden transition-all duration-500 ease-in-out">
                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Dr. Klemens Joos appointed TUM honorary professor</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>TUM awarded an honorary professor to founder and managing director of&nbsp;<a href="https://euxea.eu/index_en.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">EUXEA Holding GmbH</a>&nbsp;Dr. Klemens Joos on February 10, 2022. In doing so, TUM honors his expertise in management and politics specializing in the field of stakeholder theory and political decision-making processes as well as his excellent evaluated teaching. Joos is visiting lecturer at the TUM School of Management and teaches the Master course „Political Stakeholder Management”.</p>
<p>According to Dr. Klemens Joos it is crucial to include the relevant decision-makers of the legislative and executive branches as framework-setting secondary stakeholders in research and teaching in the long-term. This leads to a stronger focus on the importance of process competence in intermediary systems. “With Dr. Joos at the TUM School of Management we are doing important pioneering work in this area. His contributions are building bridges in Europe since the fall of the Berlin Wall”, states Dean of the TUM School of Management&nbsp;<a href="https://www.professoren.tum.de/en/friedl-gunther" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Prof. Gunther Friedl</a>.</p>
<p>Dr. Joos broad activities and experience range between business administration and political experience, starting as an advisor to a member of the European Parliament from 1988 to 1990. He founded EUTOP in 1990 realizing the potential and future that the reunification of Europe would hold. Dr. Joos has published more than 20 papers in German, English and Japanese including books and articles in applied journals. As visiting professor, Dr. Klemens Joos provides Master students with in-depth insights into the complex decision-making processes of the European Union (EU) as well as into the practice of successful lobbying especially taking into consideration the tensions between the EU institutions.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">TUM Campus Heilbronn welcomes its new professors</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p><strong>Joining us this year for their new appointments at TUM School of Management at&nbsp;</strong><a href="https://chn.tum.de/campus/student-services" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">TUM Campus Heilbronn</a><strong>&nbsp;are Prof. Dr.&nbsp;Martin Meißner&nbsp;and Prof. Dr.&nbsp;Chengguang Li.&nbsp;</strong></p>
<p>Prof. Dr.&nbsp;Martin Meißner&nbsp;is joining the TUM Campus Heilbronn as Professor of Digital Marketing at the&nbsp;<a href="/center-for-digital-transformation" target="_blank">Center for Digital Transformation</a>. Prof. Meißner studied Business Administration at Bielefeld University and subsequently finished his PhD thesis on Preference Measurement for Complex Products at the Chair of Marketing at Bielefeld University. He then received a grant from the DFG for a research stay at Monash University in Melbourne, Australia. Subsequently, he worked as an Associate Professor of Marketing at the University of Southern Denmark, during which time, he also got an Adjunct Senior Lecturer position at Monash University. Before joining the TUM School of Management, he held the Chair of Marketing at the Department of Business and Economics at Zeppelin University.</p>
<p>oining Prof. Dr. Martin Meißner at the TUM Campus Heilbronn is Prof. Dr.&nbsp;Chengguang Li&nbsp;as Professor of Strategic Management at the&nbsp;Global Center for Family Enterprise. Prior to joining TUM, he was an Assistant Professor at Ivey Business School, a Postdoctoral Fellow and project leader for the Industry 4.0 initiative of the German Federal Ministry (BMBF) in Paderborn, and a consultant at the Boston Consulting Group and Roland Berger in Berlin, Munich, and Dubai. His research interests lie in the fields of global strategy, mergers and acquisitions, and strategic alliances and joint ventures, and examines the impact of contextual factors, such as the cultural environment, on multinational enterprise strategies.</p>
<p>Congratulations on your new appointments and best of luck in your future endeavors here at the TUM School of Management!</p>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Winners of Best Teaching Award 2021</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p><strong>Each year the TUM School of Management pays tribute to lecturers who have proven outstanding teaching practices with the Best Teaching Award. The award honors their dedication and gives credit to their professional excellence. This year´s award took place in a small ceremony at the Dean´s office as the hygiene regulations during the Tag der Fakultät (Graduation Ceremony) would not allow for it.</strong></p>
<p>The Best Teaching Award is awarded in three categories according to class size.</p>
<p>The Best Teaching Award in the category large-sized classes goes to&nbsp;<a href="https://www.professoren.tum.de/kurschilgen-michael" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Prof. Michael Kurschilgen</a>&nbsp;and&nbsp;<a href="https://www.ep.mgt.tum.de/ep/team/post-doctoral-researchers/dr-christian-feilcke/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Dr. Christian Feilcke</a>. Prof. Kurschilgen is professor for managerial economics at TUM School of Management since November 2015. Dr. Christian Feilcke is Academic Councilor at the Chair of Economics since 2012. Both had won the Best Teaching Award in previous years.</p>
<p>The Best Teaching Award in the category middle-sized classes goes to&nbsp;<a href="https://www.professoren.tum.de/en/loos-benjamin" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Prof. Benjamin Loos</a>&nbsp;and&nbsp;<a href="https://www.fa.mgt.tum.de/controlling/lehrstuhlteam/mitarbeiter/yanis-gamarra-msc/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Yanis Gamarra</a>. Professor Loos studies behavioral and household finance with a particular focus on financial advice, (digital) product innovations like ETFs, fintech and individual investor behavior in general. Yanis Gamarra is Research Assistant and Doctoral Candidate at the Chair of Controlling.</p>
<p>The Best Teaching Award in the category small-sized classes goes to&nbsp;<a href="https://www.professoren.tum.de/en/maume-philipp" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Prof. Philipp Maume</a>,&nbsp;<a href="https://www.ep.mgt.tum.de/cem/schwenen/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Prof. Sebastian Schwenen</a>&nbsp;und&nbsp;<a href="https://www.professors.wi.tum.de/fileadmin/w00bca/ent/Heyde_01.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Franziska Heyde</a>. Prof. Philipp Maume’s field of research is the law of capital markets and capital market-oriented companies, of particular interest is the law of financial technology. Prof. Maume had won the Best Teaching Award in previous years. Prof. Sebastian Schwenen is Assistant Professor in Economics of Energy Markets and also affiliated as Research Fellow to the German Institute for Economic Research DIW Berlin and to the Mannheim Institute for Sustainable Energy Studies. Franziska Heyde is coach and lecturer for Entrepreneurship at UnternehmerTUM since 2011, a non-profit organization and leading center for innovation and business creation in Europe.</p>
<p>The Best Teaching Award is being awarded annually since 2013 but had to be cancelled in 2020 due to COVID-19 as the evaluation of the summer semester 2020 was not conducted by TUM CST. The assessment of the winners takes into consideration the class size, the courses grades and teachers grades based on the student´s&nbsp;evaluation from the previous winter and summer semesters.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">AdONE secures second funding period</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p><strong>Research Training Group&nbsp;</strong><strong>Advanced Optimization in a Networked Economy</strong></p>
<p>The&nbsp;<a href="https://www.dfg.de/service/presse/pressemitteilungen/2021/pressemitteilung_nr_45/index.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">German Research Foundation (DFG)</a>&nbsp;has awarded another 3 Million Euros to the Technical University of Munich (TUM) based&nbsp;<a href="https://www.gs.tum.de/en/adone/start/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Research Training Group AdONE GRK 2201</a>&nbsp;(Advanced Optimization in a Networked Economy). This enables AdONE to support the next generation of scientists for an additional 4.5 years.</p>
<p>Scientists and Doctoral students of the&nbsp;<a href="/" target="_blank">TUM School of Management</a>&nbsp;as well as the Departments of&nbsp;<a href="https://www.ma.tum.de/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Mathematics</a>&nbsp;and<a href="https://www.in.tum.de/startseite/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">&nbsp;Informatics</a>&nbsp;are members of the Research Training Group AdONE.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Optimization of logistics, transport, and mobility</strong></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Since 2017, the participating researchers and doctoral students have been working together to develop innovative mathematical methods for the optimal allocation and coordination of resources in modern logistics networks, transportation, and mobility systems.</p>
<p>With applications in airport operations, auction mechanisms, autonomous mobility, car sharing systems, production planning, vehicle routing, or warehousing, AdONE creates the scientific foundations for the continued economic success of many companies in a rapidly changing economic environment.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Interdisciplinary doctoral program AdONE</strong></p>
<p>Doctoral students receive optimal conditions for their doctorate within the framework of the Research Training Group: Embedded in a large research project and an interdisciplinary network of scientists, they can focus on their research and receive financial support for three years.</p>
<p>At the same time, they undergo a qualification program that supports them in their research and prepares them for various career paths through the acquisition of interdisciplinary skills. The Research Training Group AdONE also provides other doctoral students with similar interests access to its network and events.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">TUM School of Management among the best European Business Schools according to Financial Times</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>The TUM School of Management was placed among the top three Business Schools at a Technical University with an overall 70th place moving up six ranks since 2019. The&nbsp;<a href="https://rankings.ft.com/rankings/2869/european-business-school-rankings-2021" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Financial Times</a>&nbsp;ranks European Business Schools according to their management programs available. Our Master in Management and Technology was even ranked TOP 40 in Europe. Furthermore, the TUM School of Management offers two double degree programs with the best-ranked Business School in Europe, the HEC Paris.</p>
<p>The HEC Paris-TUM’s unique&nbsp;double degree program&nbsp;for the&nbsp;<a href="https://www.lll.tum.de/master-management-innovation/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Master in Management &amp; Innovation</a>&nbsp;and the&nbsp;<a href="/programs/master-in-management-technology" target="_blank">Master in Management &amp; Technology</a>&nbsp;(MMT) build on our mutual strengths in management and innovation as well as the interface to technology.</p>
<p>This is the 18th annual Financial Times ranking of European business schools. It is a composite ranking based on the combined performance of Europe’s leading schools across the five main rankings of programs published by the FT in 2021: MBA, Executive MBA, Masters in Management (MiM) and in 2020 for the two rankings of non-degree executive education programs. The ranking measures the schools’ quality and breadth of programs as well the diversity of their faculty.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Celebrating Graduation Day against all odds</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>The last exams have been conducted, the thesis has been handed in – an important milestone has been reached as the studies end. To celebrate this crucial step in our students’ lives, TUM School of Management organized the graduation ceremony “Tag der Fakultät” on November 26, 2021. It was the first time that the graduation had taken place since COVID-19 and after last year´s graduation had to be canceled.</p>
<p>This year, with very strict COVID19-restrictions, the Graduation Ceremony for graduates of the Bachelor’s and Master’s degree programs joyfully took place at the Audimax of the Technical University of Munich. All our graduates were excited to attend the ceremony and prepared their graduation caps. Our Dean&nbsp;<strong>Prof. Gunther Friedl</strong>&nbsp;welcomed the graduates and their families, who were watching the live stream as only the graduates were allowed to participate in the ceremony. He encouraged everyone to live the entrepreneurial spirit.&nbsp;<strong>Prof. Ernstberger</strong>&nbsp;welcomed the bachelor graduates by reminiscent his TUM graduation 20 years ago.</p>
<p>During the Master ceremony, the Peter-Pribilla Award was handed to the outstanding master thesis written in&nbsp;2020&nbsp;and&nbsp;2021&nbsp;by the founding Dean of the TUM School of Management&nbsp;<strong>Prof. Ralf Reichwald</strong>. The 2020 Award went to&nbsp;<strong>Johannes Huber</strong>&nbsp;for his Master‘s Thesis on “The Impact of Acquisitions on Software Innovation – The Case of Open Source Software Contributors” and the award for the year 2021 went to&nbsp;<strong>Ann Sophie Köller</strong>&nbsp;for her master thesis on “Future Urban Mobility in China 2050”.</p>
<p>Furthermore, we had the honor of&nbsp;<strong>Regina Neumeyer</strong>&nbsp;from&nbsp;<a href="https://www.celonis.com/ultimate-guide/?utm_source=google&amp;utm_medium=cpc&amp;utm_campaign=dach_search_general&amp;creative=517462966494&amp;keyword=celonis&amp;matchtype=p&amp;network=g&amp;device=c&amp;_bt=517462966494&amp;_bk=celonis&amp;_bm=p&amp;_bn=g&amp;_bg=126783138852&amp;gclid=Cj0KCQiAnaeNBhCUARIsABEee8WgWKI0XfgvPZC0ZuKkXpRA3EO5fjv8B6fpsarE2I3rvrlz0laI4AQaAgv0EALw_wcB" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Celonis</a>&nbsp;giving an inspiring speech of her career! “You will struggle but keep trying!”, she advised the graduates. Celonis is a company for process mining software, which was founded back in 2011 by former TUM students. It became so successful that in June 2021, Celonis raised a $1bn series D investment at $11bn valuations, becoming New York’s and Germany’s most valuable startup according to Forbes.</p>
<p>At the end of the ceremony, the graduates were honored in a light show, showing their names and profile pictures.</p>
<p><strong>Congratulations to all our graduates, we wish you a lot of success for your future!</strong></p></div>

                                    <div class="text-content relative pl-8 pt-8 pb-6 pr-6 h-[356px] md:h-[320px] overflow-hidden transition-all duration-500 ease-in-out">
                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Leveraging the latest advances in Natural Language Processing</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p><strong>On November 18/19, 2021, an inspiring workshop on Textual Analysis and Natural Language Processing (NLP) was held at&nbsp;</strong><a href="https://chn.tum.de/campus/student-services" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">TUM Campus Heilbronn</a><strong>. Leading researchers and doctoral students from the fields of management, finance, and computer science accepted the invitation of&nbsp;Sebastian Müller, Professor of Finance at the&nbsp;</strong><a href="/center-for-digital-transformation" target="_blank">Center for Digital Transformation</a><strong>&nbsp;at the TUM School of Management.</strong></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Digital transformation brings with it a flood of data, as well as data from websites, social networks, and other platforms. Most of this data is qualitative and verbal in nature, and therefore initially eludes our quantitatively oriented methods of analysis. In order to make sense of the new data we receive through digitization, we therefore rely on modern and powerful text analytics. With the help of Natural Language Processing (NLP), researchers are able to analyze textual data using computational power. The goal of the workshop was to discuss the latest developments in this field.</p>
<p>“TUM Campus Heilbronn is a young campus that explicitly addresses the impact of digital transformation and the management of family businesses. The topic of textual analysis is closely related to digital change, so regular NLP workshops for our campus are not only appropriate, but in my view almost inevitable”, said Prof. Sebastian Müller.</p>
<p>Workshop participants did not only have the opportunity to expand their knowledge of the latest advances in Natural Language Processing, but also discussed benefits, limitations, and ethical aspects of this new technology. “I am excited about the new research ideas and potential international collaborations in the field of applied textual analysis that will emerge from this workshop”, explained Prof. Müller.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Companies confirm optimal quality of degree programs</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p><strong>Graduates of the Technical University of Munich (TUM) are in demand with companies worldwide. This is seen yet again in the latest edition of the&nbsp;<a href="https://www.employability-ranking.com/ranking" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Global University Employability Ranking</a>, in which TUM holds the number 13 position. This places it among the top four universities in Europe.</strong></p>
<p>The ranking determines which universities are educating the best graduates from the point of view of employers. For the latest edition, around 11,000 managers were surveyed who recruit staff internationally in 23 countries. They work in a wide range of industries and with companies of various sizes. The rankings, which are commissioned annually by the British magazine Times Higher Education (THE), are compiled by the French management consulting firm Emerging and the German market research institute Trendence.</p>
<p>TUM has been well ahead of all other German universities for years. In the new rankings it placed 13th and is among the top four in Europe along with the University of Cambridge (4th), the University of Oxford (8th), and the ETH Zurich (11th). In the European Union it is number one.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Students highly satisfied</strong></p>
<p>The students also rate the study conditions at TUM very highly. In the most recent CHE University Rankings, which divide German universities into three groups regarding various subjects, TUM scored dozens of placings in the top group. For these rankings, the assessments of a university’s own students are the most important factor.</p>
<p>In international rankings, where research plays a key role, TUM also achieves excellent results on a regular basis. For example, it recently placed among the 25 best universities in computer science, engineering and natural sciences in the THE World University Rankings by Subject.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">TUM School of Management honors former EU Commission President Romano Prodi</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p><strong>The TUM School of Management has awarded an honorary doctorate to former EU Commission President Romano Prodi on October 25, 2021 at the TUM Audimax. In doing so, it honored the economist and two-time Italian prime minister for his outstanding academic and political contributions to economics and European unification.</strong></p>
<p>The laudatory speech for the Doctor honoris causa was held by former Bavarian Minister President Dr. Dr. h.c. Edmund Stoiber via video message. Prodi was “one of the fathers of the reunification of the continent” due to his importance in the enlargement of the EU to include numerous Eastern European countries. EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen also sent a video message. She recalled that the euro was introduced during Prodi’s term as Commission President.</p>
<p>Prof. Gunther Friedl, Dean of the TUM School of Management, emphasized Prodi´s vision on entrepreneurship in shaping globalization and worldwide challenges such as climate change. Prodi remains committed to this field today. Prof. Thomas F. Hofmann, President of TUM, called Romano Prodi a significant change agent. “Europeans will continue to benefit from your idealism, dedication, commitment and achievements for many years to come”. Prior to the event, he visited the recently opened Munich Urban Colab, where TUM and UnternehmerTUM, the Center for Innovation and Entrepreneurship, are working with startups, experienced companies, creatives, social actors and the city of Munich on sustainable smart city innovations.</p>
<p>The ceremony included a panel discussion, where Romano Prodi, the students Fiona Burckhardt and Tamara Nauhardt as well as Prof. Eugénia da Conceição-Heldt, holder of the Chair of European and Global Governance, discussed the future of Europe. Europe’s most important task today is to maintain dialogue between the U.S. and China superpowers in the face of growing tensions, Prodi conclude.</p>
<p>Prof. Romano Prodi is considered one of the founders of the Italian school of industrial economics. He was a professor of economics and industrial policy at the University of Bologna from 1971 to 1999, and a visiting researcher at Harvard and Stanford. In addition to his outstanding academic achievements, he is also awarded an honorary doctorate for his ability to apply his scientific knowledge to social progress. Both as President of the European Commission from 1999 to 2004 and as Italian Prime Minister from 1996 to 1998 and from 2006 to 2008, he has made outstanding contributions in the fields of innovation and entrepreneurship, industrial, competition and monetary policy. In this way, he has made a significant contribution to modernizing the EU and strengthening its economy.</p></div>

In the category of Industry Income, TUM School of Management received full points and therefore is among the worldwide leaders.</p>

The indicators are weighted differently depending on the subject culture.</p>

In the “Global University Employability Ranking,” in which companies evaluate the quality of graduates, TUM ranks twelfth.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Prof. Patzelt and Prof. Achleitner among the most influential German economists</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p><strong>Who carries weight in the media, research and politics? The new&nbsp;</strong><a href="https://www.faz.net/aktuell/wirtschaft/wirtschaftswissen/f-a-z-oekonomenranking-2021-die-tabellen-17538768.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>F.A.Z. Economists Ranking 2021</strong></a><strong>&nbsp;has listed the 100 most influential economists in Germany – among them TUM School of Management professors Holger Patzelt and Ann-Kristin Achleitner.</strong></p>
<p>Prof. Dr. Patzelt, who ranks 26<sup>th</sup>&nbsp;in the overall ranking and is among the top 15 most cited researchers in scientific literature, has been a Professor of Entrepreneurship and Chair of Entrepreneurship at TUM School of Management since 2010.&nbsp;Professor Patzelt conducts research on business ventures, strategic entrepreneurship and startup failure. His work covers both psychological aspects, such as cognition and decision-making by entrepreneurs, and economic factors, such as the behavior and success of entrepreneurial organizations. At the&nbsp;<a href="https://www.professors.wi.tum.de/en/ent/home/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">TUM Entrepreneurship Research Institute</a>, he is one of the driving researchers in the field of entrepreneurship.</p>
<p>Prof. Dr. Dr. Achleitner, who ranks 87, has held the&nbsp;<a href="https://www.professors.wi.tum.de/en/ef/about-us/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Chair of Entrepreneurial Finance</a>&nbsp;and, since 2003, she has been Scientific Co-Director of the Center for Entrepreneurial and Financial Studies (CEFS) at TUM.&nbsp;Her research is focused on entrepreneurial finance with a focus on the financing of innovation, venture capital, private equity, and family businesses.</p>
<p>The FAZ ranking is based on how often economists are quoted in the media, politics, social media, science and errata, analyzed by Unicepta. The impact of their research is then derived from this.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Entrepreneurship at the TUM School of Management</strong></p>
<p>Developing an entrepreneurial mindset is a key element of our mission at the TUM School of Management. Thinking outside the box, being creative and innovative, taking risks and learning from failure, and approaching problems in a proactive way is important for any career in today’s dynamic and technology‑driven world. We educate our students and researchers on entrepreneurship in interdisciplinary and international formats. <a href="/our-stories-with-impact">Plenty of&nbsp;success stories</a>&nbsp;show that this inspires and enables our students, scientists and alumni to think and act entrepreneurially.</p></div>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">Master in Management &amp; Technology ranked in the Top 50 worldwide by Financial Times</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p>In today’s new issue of the annual&nbsp;<a href="https://rankings.ft.com/rankings/5/masters-in-management-2021" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Financial Times Masters in Management rankings</a>, TUM School of Management’s&nbsp;<a href="/programs/master-in-management-technology" target="_blank">Master in Management &amp; Technology</a>&nbsp;ranked among the top 50 programs worldwide and made a huge improvement compared to the previous ranking. The Master in Management &amp; Technology is now ranked 49<sup>th</sup>&nbsp;in the overall ranking and thereby, ranks second in Germany among the Master in Management programs offered by a public university. It is also the only program in the top group offered at the business school of a technical university in Germany.</p>
<p>In the category “value for money”, TUM School of Management is on 16<sup>th</sup>&nbsp;place in the ranking, and second in Germany.</p>
<p>“I am extremely proud to have scored such a fantastic place in this year’s FT Ranking. The strong improvement shows our commitment to our high quality approach and the value of our interdisciplinarity in teaching and research at TUM School of Management”, says Prof. Dr. Gunther Friedl, Dean of the TUM School of Management.</p>
<p>This is the 17<sup>th</sup>&nbsp;edition of the FT ranking with more than 120 Masters in Management programs included in the ranking. The rankings are calculated according to information collected through two separate surveys. The first one is completed by the business schools, the second survey by alumni who finished their master studies in 2018. Overall, 17 criteria are evaluated and weighted by the newspaper. The Financial Times’ ranking gives strong credit for high salaries and salary increases three years after completion of the master’s degree. It awards additional points for factors such as: value for money, aims achieved, gender balance and diversity of international representation among students, faculty and school advisory boards.</p>

                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">TUM among the top 10 universities in Europe</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p><strong>Latest THE Rankings released</strong></p>
<p>The Technical University of Munich (TUM) has again moved up in the respected THE World University Rankings and now ranks among the 10 best universities in Europe. In the European Union, the top rankings are held by LMU Munich and TUM.</p>
<p>Compiled by the British magazine Times Higher Education (THE), the&nbsp;<a href="https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/2022/world-ranking#!/page/0/length/25/sort_by/rank/sort_order/asc/cols/stats" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">rankings</a>&nbsp;take various factors into account: Scientists and scholars worldwide are surveyed on the research and teaching reputations of the universities. Other criteria include the number of publications per researcher, citations per publication, the teacher-student ratio, third-party funding raised from the private sector and the degree of internationalization.TUM moved up again this year, advancing to number 38. As a result, the two Munich universities (LMU: 32nd) are the EU leaders in the rankings. In Europe TUM is ranked 10th.</p>
<p>In the most recent&nbsp;<a href="https://www.tum.de/en/about-tum/news/press-releases/details/36273" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">THE World University Rankings by Subject</a>, TUM is placed 14th in computer science, 24th in engineering, 25th in physical sciences (comprising most natural sciences subjects) and 46th in life sciences. TUM also regularly achieves excellent results in other international rankings, including 12th place worldwide in the&nbsp;<a href="https://www.tum.de/en/about-tum/news/press-releases/details/36330" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Global University Employability Ranking</a>, in which companies rate the quality of graduates.</p>

                                    <div class="text-content relative pl-8 pt-8 pb-6 pr-6 h-[356px] md:h-[320px] overflow-hidden transition-all duration-500 ease-in-out">
                                        <p class="text-overline1 font-bold mb-2">“Shanghai Ranking”: TUM improves once again</p>
                                        <div class="content"><p><strong>TUM climbs higher as best German technical university</strong></p>
<p>The Technical University of Munich (TUM) has further improved its standing in the current “Shanghai Ranking” (Academic Ranking of World Universities). It remains the best German technical university and is among the six top technical universities worldwide. This year TUM climbed to number 52 in the global ranking of all universities, moving up two positions. TUM is one of only four German universities to make the ranking’s top 100, together with Ludwig-Maximilians-University Munich (48), Heidelberg University (57) and the University of Bonn (84). TUM also enjoys a leading position within the EU, ranked eighth.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>“Shanghai Ranking” Criteria</strong></p>
<p>The annual “Shanghai Ranking” evaluates the worldwide research performance of universities. Also known as the “Academic Ranking of World Universities”, it was developed at the Shanghai Jiao Tong university. Central evaluation criteria are the number of publications in important academic journals such as “Nature” and “Science”, the citation rate of academics at the respective university as well as the number of Nobel Prizes and Fields Medals (The Fields Medal is one of the highest distinctions in mathematics).</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>TUM ranks in the top 50 in nine subjects</strong></p>
<p>The 2021 “Shanghai Ranking” even places the Technical University of Munich (TUM) among the 50 best universities in the world in nine different subjects:</p>
<p>•&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Remote Sensing: 5 (in Germany: 1)<br> •&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Environmental Sciences and Engineering: 15 (in Germany: 1)<br> •&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Aerospace Engineering: 17 (in Germany: 1)<br> •&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Electrical and Electronic Engineering: 19 (in Germany: 1)<br> •&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Medical Technology: 21 (in Germany: 2)<br> •&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Food Science and Technology: 37 (in Germany: 1)<br> •&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Agricultural Sciences: 38 (in Germany: 2)<br> •&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Biotechnology: 49 (in Germany: 1)<br> •&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Human Biological Sciences: 50 (in Germany: 6)</p>
<p>TUM also regularly scores very well in other international rankings. The “QS World University Ranking” declared TUM the best university in Germany for the seventh time in a row. The ranking rated TUM third among universities in the European Union and included TUM among the 50 best universities in the world.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
